title: Harvest Festival
strapline: Baskets brimming with pumpkins, apples, wheat and bread — saying thank you for the food the earth has grown.
intent: Harvest is a season of gratitude for the food that has grown and been gathered in, and a chance for children to connect what they eat with the soil, the seasons and the people who grow it.
Handling, sorting and displaying real fruit, vegetables, grains and bread grows knowledge of where food comes from and of the autumn season.
Sorting, counting, weighing and comparing the harvest is rich, hands-on mathematics with irresistible real material.
The theme of gratitude and giving to others — sharing the harvest, thinking of those with less — grows kindness, generosity and community spirit.
Children build vocabulary and real-world knowledge — harvest, crop, wheat, ripe, gather, thankful, share, plenty.
Grinding wheat, baking bread and preparing food connects the whole story from field to table in one memorable arc.
implementation: Gather a real harvest display — pumpkins, apples, corn, wheat, root vegetables, loaves — and let children handle, sort, arrange and talk about it all.
Trace where the food comes from: 'This bread was once wheat growing in a field — shall we grind some grains and see?'
Bring in maths naturally — weigh the pumpkins, sort the apples by size, count the corn cobs, line the vegetables up biggest to smallest.
Model gratitude and giving: talk about saying thank you for food, and where you can, gather items to donate to a food bank or share with others.
Offer harvest cooking — bread, soup, apple crumble — so children take the food all the way from crop to plate (checking allergies).
Link it to your own growing — what you planted and harvested from the garden — and to the turning autumn season around you.
key_questions: This bread was once wheat growing in a field — shall we grind some grains and see?
How much do you think this pumpkin weighs?
Can you line the vegetables up biggest to smallest?
Who could we share our harvest with?
How many corn cobs are in the basket?

impact.text: Children connect what they eat to the soil, the seasons and the people who grow it.
Children handle, sort and display real produce, growing knowledge of food and the autumn season.
Children sort, count, weigh and compare the harvest — rich, hands-on mathematics.
Children think of gratitude and giving — sharing the harvest with those who have less.
Children grind wheat, bake and cook, tracing the whole story from field to table.

enhancements: A real harvest display — pumpkins, apples, corn, wheat, loaves — to handle and sort.
Grinding wheat grains to connect the loaf to the field.
A food-bank collection so the giving is real.
Harvest cooking — bread, soup, apple crumble — checking allergies.
A link to the setting's own growing and the turning autumn season.

playing_exploring: Children handle, sort and explore real fruit, vegetables and grains, following their curiosity about the food and where it came from.
They use all their senses to investigate the harvest — weight, smell, texture, taste.
active_learning: Children see the food story through from grinding grain to baking bread, absorbed in the real, worthwhile work.
creating_thinking: Children sort, weigh and compare the harvest, and make links from the food on the table back to the field and the season.
